summary: The test suite covers all major requirements (manifest parsing, license classification, report generation, workflow structure) with well-organized cycles. Strengths: clear naming, good fixture approach, tests both package.json and requirements.txt, verifies all three classification states (approved/denied/unknown), tests --strict flag, includes workflow structure validation, and uses actionlint. Weaknesses: limited edge case coverage (no tests for empty/malformed manifests, special characters, missing DB/policy files in error paths); error handling for jq/dependency availability not tested; workflow.bats uses grep patterns that could be fragile (indentation-sensitive); tests don't verify policy/DB file errors are caught in all contexts; missing tests for --strict with all-approved/empty manifests; workflow tests verify structure only, not actual execution behavior. The run_act_tests.sh end-to-end harness is comprehensive but exists outside the bats framework. Overall: functional test coverage of core requirements with good organization, but gaps in rigor for edge cases and error scenarios.
